scenario: A first-time interchangeable-lens-camera buyer is considering a coworker's roughly decade-old body and wants to know whether putting the same money toward a newer generation would materially improve ordinary family photography. The frozen seller corpus contains three older DSLR-era paths and three 2018 full-frame mirrorless paths, but these are unlike listings rather than a controlled test. Nikon's D7000 renewed kit page lists 799 dollars with no posted review, a 16.2MP DX CMOS sensor, six frames per second and an 18-105mm lens. Canon's EOS 7D kit page lists 899.55 dollars, a 100-percent rating over eight reviews, an 18MP APS-C sensor, nineteen AF points, eight frames per second and an 18-135mm stabilized lens. Sony's A300 body page lists 337.99 dollars with no posted review, a 10.2MP APS-C CCD, body-based stabilization and a body-only configuration. The Sony a7 III bundle lists 1,999 dollars, a 100-percent rating over two reviews, a 24.2MP full-frame sensor, ten frames per second and accessory bundle language. The Nikon Z6 bundle lists 1,728 dollars with no posted review, a 24.5MP BSI full-frame sensor, 273-point phase-detect AF, five-axis sensor-shift stabilization and an FTZ adapter. The Canon EOS R bundle lists 1,869 dollars with no posted review, a 30.3MP full-frame sensor, Dual Pixel AF, 5,655 selectable AF points, an electronic viewfinder and an EF-to-RF adapter. Model pages place the D7000 and 7D in 2010 and 2009, and the a7 III, Z6 and EOS R in 2018, so seller 'Date First Available' fields cannot be substituted for launch generation. General sources describe BSI, CMOS development, stabilization, EVF preview, rolling-shutter distortion and dynamic range. Community discussions contain both a used-prosumer recommendation and a warning that beginners can miss used defects, show substantial improvement with retained core gear plus practice and processing changes, and show a newer phone failing an older phone's close-focus expectation because the lens and mode set changed. None of these sources measures the coworker's physical unit or supplies a matched family-photo comparison of the six listings.

rules.frozen_offer_identity_condition_matrix_v: The six seller pages are frozen offer assertions, not current prices and not controlled performance results. Preserve exact SKU, title, price, rating, review count, selected body or kit configuration, included primary lens or lack of one, adapter, storage and bundle items, seller or manufacturer wording, condition wording and every absent field. Nikon D7000 SKU B08QJQF76H is a 799-dollar renewed 18-105mm kit with no posted review. Canon EOS 7D SKU B002LSI1LY is an 899.55-dollar 18-135mm kit rated 100 percent over eight reviews. Sony A300 SKU B003J9DC72 is a 337.99-dollar body page with no posted review. Sony a7 III SKU B07XDCPVSL is a 1,999-dollar body-labeled accessory bundle rated 100 percent over two reviews. Nikon Z6 SKU B0934RQLD4 is a 1,728-dollar body and FTZ adapter bundle with no posted review and international-model wording. Canon EOS R SKU B09RTQ2VXP is a 1,869-dollar body, mount-adapter and 128GB-card bundle with no posted review. Do not compare body-only and lens-included prices as complete systems until equivalent task lenses, condition and missing costs are resolved.
rules.model_release_listing_date_boundary_v1: Model history and seller listing metadata answer different questions. The D7000 page identifies a 2010 model and the 7D page identifies an October 2009 model; the a7 III, Z6 and EOS R pages place those systems in 2018. A seller page's later 'Date First Available' value belongs to that frozen listing and does not prove the model launch date, manufacture date, firmware age, usage age or condition of the coworker's unit. Match the exact model and variant, then record serial, firmware, shutter count and physical inspection separately.
rules.generation_feature_mechanism_boundary_v1: Describe generational changes by mechanism and tested consequence. BSI rearranges sensor layers to increase captured light and can improve low-light performance, but does not quantify a gain for these exact units. CMOS capability improved over time, but sensor size, pixel count, readout, processing, lens and exposure remain separate factors. AF point counts, coverage, phase or contrast detection, face or eye tracking and burst rates are capability descriptors, not measured keeper rates. Stabilization reduces blur from ordinary camera shake but does not stop subject motion. EVFs can preview exposure, white balance and focus aids but may have display dynamic-range or latency limits. Rolling readout can distort moving subjects or flashes. Dynamic range concerns recoverable luminance range and noise, not a universal image-quality score.
rules.used_unit_inspection_gate_v1: Before purchase, verify exact body and regional variant, serial and ownership, firmware, shutter or actuation count where available, sensor condition, mount and contacts, stabilization operation, AF consistency, card slots, ports, dials, buttons, screens or viewfinder, flash, battery health, charger, clock retention, overheating or error history, weather or impact signs and return or service terms. Mount the intended lens, make native RAW and JPEG files across apertures and shutter speeds, inspect full-resolution files for dead or hot pixels, banding, oil or dust, focus inconsistency and corruption, and price missing batteries, storage, adapters, lens service and expected repair. A failed identity, safety, file-integrity or serviceability check blocks purchase rather than inviting an assumed discount.
rules.complete_kit_cost_gate_v1: Compare complete working paths rather than body stickers. For every candidate, include a lens that covers the declared family tasks at a comparable field of view and effective aperture, a healthy battery and charger, storage, required mount adapter, straps or support actually needed, taxes or delivery, immediate service, and a predeclared allowance for missing return rights or expected repair. Keep third-party accessory lenses and adapters distinct from native primary lenses, verify that autofocus, stabilization and aperture control survive any adapter, and do not treat a memory-card or accessory-heavy bundle as a complete optical path. Compute incremental cost only after the physical used unit passes inspection and every path is made task-equivalent.
rules.task_matched_family_photo_trial_v1: After the unit gate passes, compare complete paths on predeclared family tasks: a daylight portrait, a dim stationary indoor subject, a moving child or pet, a close tabletop subject and a short handheld walking or panning video. Where a body-generation claim is at issue, match lens field of view and effective aperture as closely as practical, viewpoint, distance, illumination, subject path, output dimensions, display or print size and operator practice. Record focus acquisition and keeper rate, motion blur, camera-shake blur, highlight clipping and shadow noise, color, rolling-shutter skew, video stability, start-to-shot delay, battery drain, carry weight and transfer time. Blind the final outputs when possible, preserve native files and repeat enough trials to distinguish a stable gain from chance.
rules.community_scope_boundary_v1: The used-gear discussion supplies opposing anecdotes: one commenter prefers older prosumer gear, another warns that beginners may be scammed or miss defects, and another says an old 5D Mark II can still make good stills. The telescope thread changes practice, tracking, Barlow choice, capture count and processing while retaining the core telescope, so it shows why experience and workflow are confounders rather than proving hardware irrelevance. The phone thread reports a newer model failing an older model's five-inch close-focus expectation and discusses missing telephoto or macro paths and greater minimum focus distance, so it motivates a task-specific close-focus check rather than a universal regression claim.
rules.incremental_value_decision_v1: Do not issue a general old-versus-new verdict from age, megapixels, seller prices or feature counts. After identity and complete-kit pricing, require each mandatory family task to clear its predeclared keeper-rate, blur, noise, highlight, close-focus, video-skew, stability, battery, handling and workflow threshold. Compute incremental delivered cost over the verified used path only for capabilities that produce a repeatable threshold-crossing gain. Choose the lowest total-cost complete path that passes every mandatory task. If the old body passes, prefer it unless a newer path's incremental gain clears a predeclared value threshold. If no single path passes, keep separate validated tools, borrow or rent for exceptional tasks, continue with an existing phone, or defer.
